summary: Added sales_ops_funcoes + sales_ops_person_funcoes with composite (org_id, fk) FKs, migration 0012 seeding/backfilling the legacy booleans into assignments, funcoes CRUD, and set-replace funcao assignment on the existing /people endpoints; the three booleans stay as derived deprecated mirrors. Remediation attempt 1 fixed the three Gate 2 defects: two unique-violation races that surfaced as HTTP 500, and a contactEmail clearing regression.
migration: apps/api/drizzle/0012_sales_ops_funcoes.sql, journal idx 12, tag 0012_sales_ops_funcoes, when 1785369675084 (> 0011's 1785349621521). Unchanged by the remediation - no schema change was needed, all three defects were in the service layer. drizzle-kit emitted the two composite FKs BEFORE the unique indexes they target, which would have failed on apply; hand-reordered to DDL -> indexes -> FKs -> RLS -> admin context -> seeds -> backfill.

mutations_observed: Original cycle, all restored byte-identical: 1) TENANT ISOLATION - removing eq(orgId) from listFuncoes initially SURVIVED because FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY under the non-superuser fxl_sales_test role was masking the service filter; I added 'scopes every funcoes and pessoas read by orgId even when RLS is not doing the scoping', which drives the service over an app.fxl_admin connection where the admin policy exposes every org, and the mutation then fails 'expected false to be true'. The verifier independently confirmed this technique catches 4 of 5 deleted filters, the fifth being a provably equivalent mutant. 2) COMPOSITE FK - downgraded to single-column FOREIGN KEY (funcao_id): cross-org assignment ACCEPTED, test red 'promise resolved "[]" instead of rejecting'. 3) BACKFILL - deleting the is_finder INSERT reddened 3 integration tests plus the unit contract test ('expected 4 to be greater than or equal to 5'), so both gates catch it; narrowing the org registry to sales_ops_settings alone reddened 7 of 8 migration tests. 4) IS_SYSTEM - neutralising the guard reddened the rename/archive test; dropping the CHECK constraint reddened the raw-SQL test.
remediation:
All three Gate 2 defects fixed, each with a regression test whose inversion I applied and watched go Red myself, then restored and confirmed service.ts byte-identical at sha256 2755f723b5b5c1619fb8529af502ed409823bd03807d33452ca082216a6cbc83.

DEFECT 1 (createFuncao/updateFuncao TOCTOU -> 500 instead of 409). FIX: createFuncao keeps findFuncaoClash as a fast path purely for the error message, but the INSERT now carries a bare .onConflictDoNothing(); on no returned row it re-probes under a fresh statement snapshot (READ COMMITTED gives a new snapshot per statement, so the committed winner is visible) and returns 'duplicate' or 'duplicate_slug'. UPDATE has no conflict clause, so updateFuncao runs its write inside a SAVEPOINT (a nested drizzle transaction) and maps the unique violation via a new mapFuncaoUniqueViolation() keyed on constraint name - sales_ops_funcoes_org_name_idx -> 'duplicate', sales_ops_funcoes_org_slug_idx -> 'duplicate_slug' - so both 409 reasons stay independently reachable and the surrounding transaction stays usable. TESTS (new file apps/api/test/rls/funcoes-concurrency.test.ts, pool of 16 so the calls genuinely overlap): 'resolves concurrent createFuncao calls for the same name to one row plus 409 sentinels, never an unhandled error' (12 orgs x 4 parallel, asserts zero unhandled errors, every outcome is a row or one of the two sentinels, exactly one winner per org, and the org ends with exactly one funcao) and 'resolves concurrent updateFuncao renames onto the same name to 409 sentinels, never an unhandled error' (10 orgs x 3 funcoes all renamed onto 'Product Owner' at once, and asserts the losers are left untouched rather than half-renamed). MUTATION + RED I OBSERVED: reverting createFuncao to the plain INSERT gave '× resolves concurrent createFuncao calls ... AssertionError: a lost createFuncao race must resolve to a sentinel, not raise 23505 as an HTTP 500: expected [ ...(36) ] to deeply equal []', i.e. 36 of 48 calls raised code 23505 on sales_ops_funcoes_org_slug_idx. Separately, removing the SAVEPOINT/catch from updateFuncao gave '× resolves concurrent updateFuncao renames ... expected [ ...(16) ] to deeply equal []', 16 unhandled violations. Each mutation reddened only its own test, so the two are independent.

DEFECT 2 (on-demand legacy seed's ON CONFLICT arbiter incomplete). FIX: the seed's .onConflictDoNothing({ target: [orgId, slug] }) became a bare .onConflictDoNothing(), covering every unique index on the table rather than naming one; the existing 'concurrent writer won the race, re-read the winner' fallback is now reachable because the conflict is absorbed instead of raised. TESTS: two, because the real race is not schedulable from a test. (a) DETERMINISTIC GUARD 'absorbs a seed conflict on the name index, which a slug-only arbiter cannot see' - the admin client writes a row occupying the seed's NAME but not its SLUG (org, 'Prestador', 'prestador-legado'), which a slug-only arbiter provably cannot pre-check, then asserts createPerson({isCollaborator:true}) reports a sentinel rather than throwing, plus a positive control that renames the squatter away and shows the same call then succeeding and seeding 'prestador'. (b) REAL RACE 'resolves concurrent first person writes in a freshly provisioned org without an unhandled seed conflict' - 30 fresh orgs x 5 parallel createPerson with all three legacy booleans, asserting zero unhandled errors, every person carrying all three funcoes with all three mirrors true, and exactly one funcao per slug per org. I established the shape empirically: the window is per FRESH org (it closes once the org has its funcoes), so concentrating attempts per org does not help - 4 orgs x 24 parallel hit 0 of 96, while 30 orgs x 5 hit on 6 of 6 measured runs at 2-5 failures per run. MUTATION + RED I OBSERVED: restoring the named (org_id, slug) arbiter reddened BOTH - '× absorbs a seed conflict on the name index ... the seed must absorb the conflict and report a sentinel, never raise 23505: expected '{"code":"23505","constraint":"sales_o...' to be null' and '× resolves concurrent first person writes ... a concurrent on-demand funcao seed must absorb the conflict, not raise 23505: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []'. Isolated probes confirmed the exact constraint the verifier reported, 23505/sales_ops_funcoes_org_name_idx, and that the fixed version turns the same scenario into SENTINEL:unknown_funcao (a 400) instead of a throw (a 500).

DEFECT 3 (PATCH /people/:id stopped clearing contactEmail). CLIENT CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: apps/web/src/sales-ops/SalesOpsApp.tsx:3425 builds `contactEmail: contactEmail.trim() || undefined` and apps/web/src/sales-ops/api.ts:72 sends JSON.stringify(body), which DROPS an undefined key, so an absent key is the only way the shipped dialog can clear an e-mail. FIX: restored master's unconditional `contactEmail: data.contactEmail || null` in updatePerson, so both 'key absent' and 'key present but empty' clear, exactly as before the slice. Documented in a comment that contactEmail is a full-replace field on this endpoint and that a later slice sending funcaoIds must send contactEmail alongside. TEST: 'clears contactEmail when the Pessoa dialog omits the key, and keeps it when a value is sent' in funcoes-rls.test.ts uses the REAL wire shape - it builds the dialog's object and round-trips it through JSON.stringify/JSON.parse, then asserts `'contactEmail' in blankedWire === false` before sending it, so the test would break if the wire shape assumption ever stopped holding. It checks the returned row AND the stored contact_email column, plus positive controls that a real address round-trips, that an explicit empty string also clears, and that the e-mail write does not disturb the funcao set. MUTATION + RED I OBSERVED: reinstating the conditional spread gave '× clears contactEmail when the Pessoa dialog omits the key ... AssertionError: expected 'sig@example.com' to be null', which is precisely the verifier's reproduction.
api_contract_matches_plan: yes - unchanged by the remediation. No table name, column name, endpoint shape or 409 reason code was touched; the fixes only change how a lost race is resolved (sentinel instead of an unhandled throw) and restore a pre-existing write semantic. The two originally reported deviations stand and were judged acceptable on merit by the verifier: (a) createFuncao returns 'duplicate' for a name collision and 'duplicate_slug' for a derived-key collision, so both documented 409 reasons are reachable; (b) resolvePersonFuncoes ensures all three legacy slugs on demand, not just prestador, because 0012 only seeds orgs that existed at migration time.

notes: 1) Deliberately NOT fixed, per the coordinator: the areas-rls.test.ts RLS-masking blind spot, and the 'Meus dados shows every seller in the org' gap. Both need their own slice; the adminDb technique in funcoes-rls.test.ts is the ready-made fix for the former. 2) Mechanism of defect 2 for the record: the window is between ExecCheckIndexConstraints, which only pre-checks the ARBITER index, and the subsequent normal insertion into the non-arbiter unique indexes, where a committed conflicting row raises 23505. That window is not schedulable from a test, which is why the deterministic guard constructs the equivalent invisible-to-the-arbiter state directly. Measured at roughly 1.5% of calls / 8% of fresh orgs. 3) The fixed seed returns 'unknown_funcao' (400) rather than adopting a differently-slugged funcao that squats the seed name; adopting it would be surprising, and the contract pinned is 'never a 500'. 4) Verifier style notes left as-is deliberately: exported-but-unrouted getFuncao (staged for 07/09), an empty PATCH on a system funcao bumping updatedAt, and archived funcoes remaining assignable (needed so historical assignments keep resolving; slice 09 should decide explicitly). 5) Test DB left clean: 0 leftover org_% rows in sales_ops_people/sales_ops_funcoes and 0 orphaned rls_probe_% roles. All throwaway probe files removed. No process left running; every run was run-once.
